newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa industrial shares dive on rate hike panic.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa industrial shares dive on rate hike panic.

text.p: A one point hike in Bank and prime lending rates took a heavy toll on South African shares on Thursday.

Industrials were hit hardest, plunging 1.2 percent on the day after shedding one percent in the first 10 minutes of trade. The all-share index was dragged down with industrials while golds followed the downhill slope, too, depressed by bullion.
Gold shares softened in sympathy with diving industrials but were further eroded by a feeble bullion, which only briefly nosed above $380 an ounce before falling again.
Industrial equity futures exacted their pound of flesh from the cash market as reverse arbitrage again crept in, extending the week's theme of selling stock and buying futures.
However, the futures market did not escape unscathed as depression seized trade there, too, and kept industrial and all-share equity futures down.

But dealers said that once the initial shock of the rate hike wore off after a couple of days -- perhaps even by Monday -- shares could start coming back as bargain-hunters snapped up good buying opportunities.
But prices did not seem to be low enough yet, with institutions remaining ofn the siddelines.
Foreigners were also absent from the market, wary of possible interest rate hike hangovers, and despite a firmer rand.
Overall volumes were moderate but more than a quarter of trade was concentrated in the realms of the top five shares according to market capitalisation.
De Beers enjoyed the largest traded volume with 405,700 shares or 77 million rands worth changing hands. The diamond giant lost 300 cents or 2.1 percent of its value to 139.75 rand.

Dealers said there was a chance a firm finish on Wall Street overnight could trigger a jump up in South African shares. But they added that local stocks were very selective about when to follow and when not to follow the U.S. market's lead.
Bank shares, which should have taken heart from the rate increase which will go some way to relieve an acute squeeze on margins, find to find much consolation in the move.
The industrial index plunged 97.2 points to 7,980.1, the all-shares fell 76.5 to 6,774.4 and golds shed 7.9 to 1,704.6.
